stem: A client taking phenelzine plans to eat aged cheese and cured meats at a family event. Which teaching by the nurse is most important?

options.A: Choose small portions of the aged cheese and cured meat if the client's blood pressure is normal before the meal, because the interaction depends mainly on the amount eaten at one time.
options.B: Avoid the aged cheese and cured meats because tyramine-rich foods can interact with phenelzine and precipitate a potentially dangerous hypertensive crisis.
options.C: Skip the phenelzine dose on the morning of the event and resume it the next day, because a brief medication interruption makes the high-tyramine foods safer to eat.
options.D: Take an antacid before the meal and continue phenelzine as prescribed, because reducing gastric acidity limits tyramine absorption enough to prevent the interaction.

rationale: Current DailyMed labeling for phenelzine warns that hypertensive crises can occur when patients ingest foods containing high concentrations of tyramine. The label specifically instructs patients to avoid foods that have undergone aging, fermentation, pickling, smoking, or similar protein breakdown and lists aged cheeses and dry/cured sausages among foods to avoid. The dietary restrictions continue during therapy and for two weeks after discontinuation, so skipping a single dose does not remove the risk. Small portions based on a normal premeal blood pressure and antacid use are not label-supported methods for preventing the interaction. Therefore B is correct.
educational_objective: Teach clients taking phenelzine to avoid high-tyramine foods such as aged cheeses and dry/cured meats because the interaction can precipitate hypertensive crisis and is not prevented by a skipped dose, small portion, or antacid.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_locator: Contraindications/Warnings: hypertensive crises may be caused by foods with high tyramine or dopamine concentrations; avoid high-protein foods altered by aging, fermentation, pickling, smoking, or bacterial contamination, including cheeses especially aged varieties and dry sausage such as salami and pepperoni. Warning to the Patient: listed foods and beverages must be avoided while taking phenelzine and for two weeks after discontinuation.
source_claim_supported: Phenelzine therapy requires avoidance of high-tyramine foods such as aged cheeses and dry/cured sausages because the interaction can cause hypertensive crisis; restrictions persist for two weeks after discontinuation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed pp. 38–41: identify food-medication interactions, provide medication education, recognize adverse effects and contraindications, and implement measures that promote safe medication use.
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — phenelzine and tyramine interaction
correction_summary: Rebuilt all distractors to remove absolute-word cueing and replaced them with realistic but unsupported attempts to reduce tyramine risk through portion control, single-dose interruption, or antacid use.

audit_findings.clinical_category: MAOI therapy — tyramine food interaction and hypertensive crisis prevention
audit_findings.stem: PASS — names two label-listed high-tyramine food categories and asks a single medication-teaching decision.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — portion size may seem relevant, but the label directs avoidance rather than relying on a normal premeal blood pressure or small serving.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS — directly matches the current phenelzine dietary warning and identifies the clinically important hypertensive-crisis risk; uniquely best.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — a single missed dose does not remove the interaction risk because dietary restrictions continue for two weeks after discontinuation.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS as distractor — antacid use is not a label-supported strategy for preventing tyramine-related hypertensive crisis.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — only B follows the explicit food-avoidance instruction without adding an unsupported workaround.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A, C, and D continue the high-tyramine exposure through strategies not supported by the prescribing information.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — no distractor contains the prior absolute-word pattern and all choices are plausible self-management statements.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — NCSBN Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies directly includes food-medication interactions and medication education.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether a small portion or temporary medication interruption could be accepted; the current label explicitly instructs avoidance and extends restrictions for two weeks after discontinuation, leaving B uniquely correct.
